quality_scores.Title: A Novel Approach for Mixed-Methods Research Using Large Language Models: A Report Using Patients' Perspectives on Barriers to Arthroplasty

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: The mixed-methods thematic workflow is described, but the LLM's pattern-based process is not tied to a precise qualitative tradition.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Six interviews and one focus group are clinically relevant but small, private, and evaluated in one condition.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Chunk size and prompt wording are reported, while snapshot, parameters, complete outputs, and run code are not.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: A prior human team analysis is a useful comparator, but author overlap and nonblind visual matching limit independence.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Clinical/method experts compare outputs by all-author consensus without a formal blind rating protocol.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Overlap percentages come from subjective matching and are not a validated automatic measure.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Human and model themes are allowed to differ, yet consensus matching still centers one human codebook.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Themes are consolidated by transcript, but persistent quote-to-theme links are not reported.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Only one model run is reported.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: IRB and consent are reported, but de-identification and proprietary-service retention safeguards are not.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Prompts and a topic guide are available, while transcripts, code, exact model, and run logs are not.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: Conclusions appropriately limit the LLM to preliminary support and acknowledge lost specificity, chunking, privacy, and interpretive limits.

quality_scores.Title: Assessing the Potential and Limits of Large Language Models in Qualitative Coding

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: The fixed-code deductive task and its relationship to qualitative/quantitative ethnographic coding are explicit.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Four sessions and 990 lines support detailed testing but represent one small tutoring context and codebook.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: The exact model snapshot, temperature, prompts, context window, codebook, output rules, and analyses are reported.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Reconciled human labels and three controlled prompt regimes provide strong direct comparators.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Eleven experts assess construct properties, but they do not blindly judge model output quality.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Kappa, precision, recall, and F1 fit fixed-label coding, but do not validate interpretation and are unstable when human agreement is weak.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Reconciled binary labels assume a single answer and do not preserve plausible alternative readings.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Every prediction maps to a source line and error cases are inspected, but no generated rationale/provenance chain is evaluated.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Three runs per method and controlled context/example changes directly test some stability and prompt sensitivity.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: De-identification is reported for minor student data, while IRB, consent, and API governance are not.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Most model and prompt details are available, but restricted data and absent code prevent complete replication.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: Claims are bounded to construct- and prompt-dependent performance and the single-dataset limitation is explicit.

quality_scores.Title: Automating Thematic Analysis: How LLMs Analyse Controversial Topics

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: The paper grounds codebook development and consensus coding in thematic-analysis and reflexive/abductive practice.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: The controversial public corpus is fit for probing interpretation but contains only seventeen deliberately selected statements.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Model families, dates, temperature, main prompt, thresholds, workflow, and a second prompt/model experiment are described.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Two human coders, two initial LLMs, and three later models create informative independent and cross-model comparisons.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Author coders inspect disagreement in depth, but no external evaluator or blind protocol is used.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Agreement/correlation measure assignment overlap, while arbitrary thresholds and no human validation limit construct validity.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: The analysis explicitly treats disagreement and divergent human/model readings as analytic evidence rather than mere error.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: All source statements and statement-theme matrices are visible, providing unusually direct traceability for the pilot.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: A later model/prompt experiment probes sensitivity, but repeated stochastic runs and seeds are not reported.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: Political bias, sensitive-data transfer, de-identification effects, and accountability are discussed without a formal ethics protocol.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Prompt, statements, matrices, and toolkit are available, while complete code, API logs, and exact snapshots are not.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: The authors frame results as a non-generalizable pilot and emphasize labor, subjectivity, and model/prompt dependence.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: No fixed, enumerated evaluation dataset or sampling frame is reported.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Twenty-seven roles, algorithms, data flows, model configuration, and public code make the architecture comparatively transparent.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: No human or system baseline is evaluated.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: No reported expert, participant, or user evaluation supports effectiveness claims.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: No automatic quality metric is reported.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Agent finalization collapses outputs without testing competing interpretations.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Agents are instructed to validate against inputs, but traceability and hallucination detection are not empirically assessed.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Runs, seeds, model variance, and prompt robustness are not reported.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: Privacy and data-governance risks are acknowledged explicitly, though safeguards are left for future work.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Public code and detailed algorithms are available, despite the missing exact model snapshot and fixed test package.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: Claims of accuracy, bias reduction, speed, and cost savings are not supported by measured evaluation.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Three real HCI studies provide plausible material, while passage selection and response counts are underreported.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Models, one exact GPT snapshot, prompt structures, temperature, reference construction, and five-generation procedure are described.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: GPT-4, Llama 2, and published passages provide comparisons, but the passages are not independent gold interpretations.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: No qualitative expert or participant evaluates the generated analyses.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: SBART cosine similarity is not validated as a measure of qualitative interpretive quality.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: One selected published passage is treated as the reference and alternative valid interpretations are not assessed.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Raw responses are inputs, but generated claims are not linked back to specific evidence units.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Five outputs per item assess stochastic variation, though prompt/data-order sensitivity is not tested.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: Consent, de-identification, API handling, and other responsible-research details are not reported.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: No benchmark package, code, complete output set, or Llama snapshot is linked.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: Claims that LLMs match traditional efficacy are not justified by unvalidated embedding similarity alone.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Batching, temperature, role/context strategy, and workflow are described, while the exact snapshot and complete prompts are absent.

quality_scores.Title: Reflections on Inductive Thematic Saturation as a potential metric for measuring the validity of an inductive Thematic Analysis with LLMs

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: The phase-two inductive-coding scope is explicit, but the prompt calls codes themes and saturation is only one contested notion of quality.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Two open interview datasets with 10 and 39 cases provide relevant contrasting empirical material.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: The model family/context size, temperature, full prompts, sequential procedure, formulas, and counts are reported.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: No human saturation estimate, independent deduplicator, or alternative metric baseline is evaluated.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: No human evaluates code validity, duplicate decisions, or metric outputs.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: The proposed ratio and embedding check are not validated against human judgments and can reward repetitive generic coding.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: A single LLM decides code equivalence and no alternative codebook interpretation is retained.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Prompted participant quotations give direct intended evidence links for every generated code.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Only one order/run is reported despite explicit recognition that order and stochasticity may change saturation.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: Open-data use is stated, but source consent, de-identification, and API handling are not re-audited.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Prompts, formulas, data citation, model, and counts are available, while code and generated codebooks are not linked.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: The draft consistently presents the metric as a working hypothesis requiring validation rather than a settled quality measure.

quality_scores.Title: Scalable Qualitative Coding with LLMs: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Matches Human Performance in Some Hermeneutic Tasks

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: The nine-code socio-historical content-analysis task and the distinction between codebook construction and deductive application are explicit.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: A difficult, paragraph-level historical-news corpus with a held-out human-coded subset directly matches the claimed task.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Prompt components, codebook revisions, model/condition comparisons, parameters and output format are described and supported by an OSF package.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: A hidden human-derived gold standard and GPT-3.5/prompt ablations are useful, but the human-gold construction and independence are underreported.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Human labels support code-level agreement analysis, but no separate blind panel evaluates rationales or interpretive adequacy.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Cohen's kappa is appropriate for fixed binary codes but cannot validate rationales or establish broader qualitative quality.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: The paper explicitly recognizes manifold meaning and code-specific difficulty, while the benchmark still collapses each passage to one gold label set.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Every decision is tied to a source passage and rationales are available for error inspection.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Several prompt conditions and two model families are compared, but independent repeated runs and seeds are not reported.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: No formal ethics, privacy or responsible-research protocol is reported.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Code, data, and prompt/codebook examples are public on OSF, but exact proprietary model snapshots are not available.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: The reported case supports codebook-specific GPT-4 performance, but predictions about majority-codebook viability and human equivalence exceed one underreported gold-standard study.

quality_scores.Interpretation caution: The total is a compact audit aid, not a ranking; interpret every dimension against the paper's claim and study design.

quality_scores.Title: Thematic Analysis with Large Language Models: does it work with languages other than English? A targeted test in Italian

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: The paper invokes Braun-Clarke phases, but compares thematic analysis with Grounded Theory categories and operationalizes only phases 2–4.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Nineteen public native-language interviews and their prior QualCoder analysis directly support the multilingual research question.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Prompts, stages, temperatures and model families are described, while scripts, snapshots and complete outputs are not released.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: An independently created human analysis is relevant, but the study author manually pairs and edits labels before comparison.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: One original-study lead author provides informed scores, but a single nonblind rater cannot establish robust quality.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Sentence-embedding similarity between short, manually paired and edited labels is not validated as a measure of interpretive quality.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: The paper notes that two analysts can form different themes, but ultimately evaluates against one prior category structure.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Initial codes carry representative quotations and themes list underlying codes, providing meaningful if incomplete traceability.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Three temperature variants and one language-of-prompt check probe sensitivity, but no replicated runs or seeds are reported.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: Public data are cited, but consent, de-identification and cloud-processing governance are not re-audited.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Source data, human coding and prompt figures are available; scripts, full model outputs and exact snapshots are absent.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: Conclusions acknowledge the one-language case but still infer broader multilingual viability from Italian alone.

quality_scores.Interpretation caution: The total is a compact audit aid, not a ranking; interpret every dimension against the paper's claim and study design.

quality_scores.Title: When Qualitative Research Meets Large Language Model: Exploring the Potential of QualiGPT as a Tool for Qualitative Coding

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: Inductive and deductive coding are distinguished, but thematic rigor is represented mainly through tool features and label agreement.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Simulated and real community data cover multiple tasks, yet samples are small, partitions underdescribed and the synthetic-size reporting is difficult to reconcile.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Architecture, prompt components and workflows are described, but sampling parameters, exact snapshots, code and full run logs are unavailable.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Two human coders and several model conditions provide comparisons, although model-human equivalence decisions are produced by the same team.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Human coders negotiate labels and support comparisons, but no independent blind expert or actual user study evaluates QualiGPT outputs.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Kappa suits fixed deductive labels, but the inductive kappa depends on post-hoc semantic-equivalence judgments and does not validate insight.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Human negotiation and divergent labels are acknowledged, while evaluation still reduces interpretations to binary equivalence/agreement.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: The tool reports source quotations with themes and can export data, prompts and results together.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Three GPT-4 deductive runs demonstrate consistency, but stochastic/prompt robustness for inductive analysis is not systematically tested.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: Privacy motivates API-key control and deletion claims, but public-community consent, retention and security are not independently evaluated.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Synthetic data and prompt examples are supplied; real data, executable source, exact versions and full logs are not clearly available.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: Claims of significant improvement, expert-comparable quality and workflow revolution exceed moderate agreement and the absence of a usability study.

quality_scores.Interpretation caution: The total is a compact audit aid, not a ranking; interpret every dimension against the paper's claim and study design.

quality_scores.Title: A Large Language Model Approach to Educational Survey Feedback Analysis

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: The paper names inductive/deductive thematic analysis, but most evaluation operationalizes component NLP tasks rather than interpretive theme quality.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: A 2,500-comment real educational test set plus a separate 2,000-comment development set is large and directly relevant.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Exact snapshots, temperature, task schemas, batching, prompts, development split and component evaluations are reported.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Four expert annotators, SetFit and RoBERTa provide meaningful human and non-LLM comparisons across multiple component tasks.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Four knowledgeable annotators establish multilabel references and humans inspect errors and reasoning, although some tasks use one annotator.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Classification metrics fit fixed tasks, but the custom GPT-4 evaluator and downstream scores do not validate inductive themes.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Consensus labels collapse disagreement and the inductive workflow does not preserve alternative plausible theme structures.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Exact excerpt extraction is auditable and outputs are structured, while theme-level links and chain-of-thought faithfulness are not assured.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Temperature is fixed and retries are automatic, but no independent repeated-run, seed or order-robustness analysis is reported.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: Human-subjects determination, local name screening, restricted-data rationale and ethics-controlled access are clearly reported.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Prompts and schemas are supplemental and exact snapshots are named, while data are restricted and executable code is absent.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: Component-performance and cost conclusions are supported, but human-level and chain-of-thought-transparency claims go beyond the unvalidated thematic task.

quality_scores.Interpretation caution: The total is a compact audit aid, not a ranking; interpret every dimension against the paper's claim and study design.

quality_scores.Title: Performing an Inductive Thematic Analysis of Semi-Structured Interviews With a Large Language Model: An Exploration and Provocation on the Limits of the Approach

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: The six-phase Braun-Clarke frame is explicit, but only selected phases are emulated and the two comparator analyses use different traditions.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Two open interview datasets with 23 participants and published human analyses directly support the exploratory comparison.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Prompts, stage sequence, temperature variations, code counts, examples and an initial-coding script are reported.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Prior human analyses provide substantive comparators, but they are heterogeneous and evaluated nonblind by one author.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: No independent human evaluator or formal rating protocol assesses the generated analysis.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Theme resemblance is judged narratively without a validated automatic metric.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: The paper recognizes subjectivity and model-generated alternatives, but comparisons still privilege one published theme set per corpus.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Generated codes include representative quotations and indexed code references were introduced to reduce hallucinated assignments.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Temperature-based repeated theme generation exposes variation, although runs are not systematic and seeds are not reported.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: The paper selects anonymized open data and discusses consent/cloud-processing risks, but does not provide an operational governance protocol.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Public data, prompt text and a GitHub initial-coding script support partial reproduction, despite the missing snapshot and complete output package.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: The exploratory framing is appropriately cautious in places, but claims of viability and validity remain stronger than a sole-author thematic match warrants.

quality_scores.Interpretation caution: The total is a compact audit aid, not a ranking; interpret every dimension against the paper's claim and study design.

quality_scores.Title: Introducing ChatGPT to a researcher's toolkit: An empirical comparison between rule-based and large language model approach in the context of qualitative content analysis of political texts in Finnish

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: Qualitative content analysis and close/distant reading are described, while the benchmark itself reduces analysis to keyword/topic classification.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Finnish political texts provide valuable multilingual evidence, but the narrow subset is small and its stated document totals are internally inconsistent.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: The main prompt, platform, temperature and manual process are shown, but the exact model, corpus spreadsheet and executable procedure are unavailable.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Etuma and manual close-reading labels are relevant comparators, yet the sole author constructs and evaluates the reference.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: No independent or redundantly rated human evaluation is reported.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Precision, recall and F1 are appropriate for keyword recovery but do not validate qualitative theme interpretation.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: The paper explicitly protects researcher autonomy and nuance, though the formal evaluation uses one exhaustive keyword reference.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Outputs are stored beside source texts for manual validation, but ChatGPT supplies no rationale or durable source-link mechanism.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Repeated identical prompts reveal nonreproducibility, but the repetitions and variance are not quantified.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: Bias, misinformation, hallucination, integrity and sensitive-data risks are substantively discussed without a formal protocol.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Prompts are reported, but data, labels, code, exact model and run logs are not released.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: The conclusions are cautious, retain traditional methods and clearly connect claims to the observed precision/recall trade-off.

quality_scores.Interpretation caution: The total is a compact audit aid, not a ranking; interpret every dimension against the paper's claim and study design.

quality_scores.Title: Qualitative Code Suggestion: A Human-Centric Approach to Qualitative Coding

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: The paper models the temporal, coder-specific and rare-code properties of inductive qualitative coding rather than treating it as static classification.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Fifteen health interviews with two authentic coding histories, 63,927 words and 1,175 assignments form a directly relevant benchmark.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Data formatting, saturation splits, model architectures, hyperparameters, exact GPT snapshot, prompt and public code are detailed.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: BM25, SVM, encoder/retriever models, GPT-3.5 and original coder histories provide strong and diverse baselines.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Two experienced evaluators judge real suggestions, but each coder-specific sample appears singly rated and no deployed-user study is conducted.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: MRR/F1/P@4 suit ranking and novelty, while BERTScore-based soft NDCG is not independently validated for code meaning.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Coder-specific histories remain separate and human results empirically show several relevant alternatives beyond the original assigned codes.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Suggestions are traceable to highlighted spans, preceding questions and the exact coder-specific code history.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: All fourteen saturation points per coder are tested, but model seeds and repeated GPT runs are not reported.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: IRB approval, participant consent, sensitivity-based access and the assist-not-replace design stance are explicit.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Code, detailed hyperparameters, prompt and a mediated dataset are available, including an exact GPT checkpoint.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: Conclusions accurately foreground rare-code failure, coder-style effects, limits of automatic references and the need for applied evaluation.

quality_scores.Interpretation caution: The total is a compact audit aid, not a ranking; interpret every dimension against the paper's claim and study design.

quality_scores.Title: Decoding Complexity: Exploring Human-AI Concordance in Qualitative Coding

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: Semantic and latent coding are distinguished, but task complexity simultaneously changes segment length, codebook size and interpretive depth.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Real German interviews are appropriate, while segments are researcher-selected and per-task sample counts/data access are unreported.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Prompt structure, conditions and temperature are shown, but snapshots, full data, outputs and code are absent.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Two human coders and two LLMs provide direct comparisons, though the reconciled human reference is not independent of codebook construction.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Human-human agreement is reported, but no external qualitative evaluator inspects model errors or latent interpretations.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Kappa fits fixed multi-label code application but cannot capture qualitative depth, as the authors themselves acknowledge.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Unified human annotations collapse disagreement and alternative interpretations are not preserved.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Assignments remain attached to source segments, but no rationale or evidence-faithfulness analysis is provided.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Zero/one/few-shot conditions test example sensitivity, while repeated stochastic runs and seeds are absent.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: Confidentiality and researcher-subjectivity risks are discussed, but no ethics approval, consent or API safeguard is reported.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Only an appendix prompt is available; data, labels, code, model snapshots and outputs are not released.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: As a preliminary short paper, conclusions remain task-specific and explicitly reject using IRR alone as a complete quality measure.

quality_scores.Interpretation caution: The total is a compact audit aid, not a ranking; interpret every dimension against the paper's claim and study design.

quality_scores.Title: Discovering Latent Themes in Social Media Messaging: A Machine-in-the-Loop Approach Integrating LLMs

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: The paper distinguishes topics and themes and invokes thematic analysis, but the operational method is chiefly clustering, summarization and classification.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Two public, large, substantively important ad corpora totaling more than 31,000 documents are well matched to scalable theme discovery.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: The iterative pipeline, prompts, thresholds, K values, examples, datasets and code repository are clearly documented.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: SBERT, LDA, BERTopic, pre-existing themes and human judgments provide diverse direct comparisons.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Expert coherence/summary checks and large mapping samples are valuable, but annotator overlap, independence and reliability are underreported.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Accuracy/F1 fit theme assignment and correlations characterize use, while they do not establish validity of the generated theme ontology.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: The system converges on one merged theme set and does not preserve alternative expert or model interpretations.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Clusters and ads remain linkable and summaries use representative members, but exhaustive claim-to-ad provenance is not evaluated.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Two iterations and two datasets probe some robustness, while K/threshold/order sensitivity, seeds and repeated GPT runs are absent.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: An ethics statement and bias/demographic-subjectivity limitations are present, but affected communities and targeting harms are not directly evaluated.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Code, public data, prompt templates and technical settings are available; the exact GPT snapshot and seeds are missing.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: Performance and scalability claims are supported, while 'cleaner/more explainable' qualitative claims rely on limited nonindependent validation.

quality_scores.Interpretation caution: The total is a compact audit aid, not a ranking; interpret every dimension against the paper's claim and study design.

quality_scores.Title: Prompts Matter: Comparing ML/GAI Approaches for Generating Inductive Qualitative Coding Results

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: The study explicitly translates Grounded Theory line-by-line and verb-phrase practices into distinct inductive prompting conditions.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: The 127-message community case is authentic and fully displayed, but too small and singular for broad performance claims.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Four approaches, prompt adaptations, data and complete generated codebooks are documented in extensive appendices.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: BERTopic, chunk/item prompt variants and four human codebooks offer meaningful methodological comparisons.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Two authors independently inspect every codebook and four humans code the corpus, but agreement and blind/external evaluation are absent.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Code counts and manually flagged issues are not validated automatic measures of inductive insight or usefulness.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Insider and outsider human codebooks plus machine-only discoveries make interpretive differences visible rather than assuming one gold answer.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Full input messages and generated codebooks permit direct grounding inspection.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Only one run per approach is reported, with no temperature, seeds or stochastic robustness assessment.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: Anonymization is visible, but ethics review, consent, community governance and API privacy are not reported.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Data and prompts/outputs are appended, while executable code, exact snapshot and run metadata are unavailable.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: The authors appropriately reject human-imitation claims and frame results as one-context evidence requiring theory-informed human-AI evaluation.

limitations: All included evidence records are based on inspected complete text; title/abstract screening alone was never used for extraction.
The union contains 38 scoped records without abstracts; no-abstract titles that plausibly met scope were routed to retrieval, and no extraction was made from title evidence alone.
Records whose complete text could not be retrieved remain explicit nonretrievals and are not counted as included.
Subscription and access failures prevented complete inspection of several forward-chain candidates.
Publication-family links are reviewer judgments based on matching titles, abstracts, methods, and official publication histories and should remain visible in downstream deduplication.
